definitions.definition: componentwise sum of second spatial derivatives

inputs.statement: For all x,r>0 there exists a∈R with u_tt−Δ_xu=a u.

For measurable topological X with measurable opens, normed additive commutative V, measure μ finite on compacts and continuous compactly supported f:X→V, f is integrable.

inputs.statement: Continuous functions on compact sets in uniform spaces are uniformly continuous there.

output.statement: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

argument.text: Fix r>0, set J=[r/2,3r/2], and choose C_J by H003. Smoothness and constancy imply all derivatives vanish outside C_J and on its boundary. Thus e(·,r) is continuous and compactly supported; M001 proves integrability. Choose box B containing C_J. M004 gives uniform continuity of e_t on B×J. M002 expresses time difference quotients as interval averages of e_t; uniform convergence and finite measure give E'(r)=∫_B e_t.

Product differentiation gives e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ(∂_j u)·∂_j u_t. For each j the scalar function u_t·∂_j u is smooth compactly supported; its j derivative is (∂_j u_t)·∂_j u+u_t·∂²_j u, integrable by M001. Coordinate permutation and M003 give Fubini. M002 on a large interval gives zero integral of that derivative from endpoint values. Summing yields E'=2∫u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu). Differentiating H001 gives u·u_t=0; H002 gives acceleration parallel to u, so integrand zero. Thus E'=0; r arbitrary.

applications.bindings: α=R^(n−1); β=R; μ,ν Lebesgue; V=R; f=coordinate-permuted derivative.
hypothesis_checks: Measurable Euclidean factors and S-finite measures.
